questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) Each of the boys / (B) have done / (C) their homework / (D) No error
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Each' is singular; it takes a singular verb. 'have done' should be 'has done'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) I am reading / (B) this book / (C) since two hours / (D) No error
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Since' marks a point in time; 'for' marks a duration. Correct: 'for two hours'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) She is one of the best students / (B) who has worked hard / (C) in the school / (D) No error
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Who' refers to 'students' (plural), so the verb should be 'have worked', not 'has worked'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) He told me / (B) that he will / (C) come tomorrow / (D) No error
questions.explanation: B is correct. In reported speech, when the main verb is past ('told'), the reported clause shifts: 'will' → 'would'. Correct: 'that he would come'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) Neither Ravi / (B) nor his friends / (C) was present at the meeting / (D) No error
questions.explanation: C is correct. With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject — 'friends' (plural), so 'was' should be 'were'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) One should / (B) always do / (C) his best / (D) No error
questions.explanation: C is correct. When 'one' is the subject, the possessive must also be 'one's', not 'his'. Correct: 'one's best'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) The list of items / (B) are placed / (C) on the table / (D) No error
questions.explanation: B is correct. The subject is 'list' (singular), not 'items' (part of a prepositional phrase). 'are' should be 'is placed'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) The police / (B) have arrested / (C) the thief / (D) No error
questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Police' is a collective noun treated as plural in standard English → 'have arrested' is correct. No error.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) The manager along with / (B) his staff members / (C) are attending the conference / (D) No error
questions.explanation: C is correct. Phrases like 'along with', 'together with', 'as well as' do not change the number of the subject. The subject is 'manager' (singular), so 'are attending' should be 'is attending'.

questions.stem:
Find the part with the grammatical error:
(A) Scarcely had / (B) she finished speaking / (C) than the audience applauded / (D) No error
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Scarcely/Hardly...when/before' is the correct construction. 'Than' is used with 'no sooner...than'. Correct: 'when the audience applauded'.
